title: Handoff latency mystery - notebook
content:
Purpose: random scratchpad for the weird regional handoff latency spike on 2026-03-09. Not formal—notes to self, commands tried, quick hypotheses, and next actions. Keep messy.

Summary (short):
- Customer-facing API saw 3x tail latency increase for a 30m window across eu-west and us-east during sustained traffic transfer.
- Symptoms: requests accepted by control plane, forwarded to an egress cluster that took ~250-700ms extra in total time; observed more inflight retries + extra KV cache misses.
- Automated rollback (fallback to small-model variant in local tier) reduced tail but didn't fully eliminate sporadic ~200ms bumps.

Timeline snippets (local times):
- 2026-03-09 13:02 UTC: first alert (latency p95 across route /v1/generate jumped to 540ms).
- 2026-03-09 13:07 UTC: routing policy attempted regional shift (weight move eu-west -> eu-central for 20% traffic).
- 2026-03-09 13:08-13:35 UTC: repeated backoff/retries on the handoff path; increased egress queue length.
- 2026-03-09 13:36 UTC: canary rollback to previous routing policy; p95 dropped to baseline ~180ms by 13:45.

Quick reproduction attempts (commands I ran):
1) curl trace through the control plane (local test cluster):
   curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer TEST" -H "X-Region: eu-west" \
     "https://api.internal.redwood/generate?model=redwood-small" 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p'
   -> observed: control-plane accept, then 502 upstream reset returned after ~580ms.

2) routectl inspect (internal tool):
   routectl get routes --route-id r123 --verbose --since "2026-03-09T13:00Z"
   -> output: multiple rapid policy updates (policy-version bumped 3x), some nodes showing policy-applied=false for 12s windows.

3) egress debug logs (via gcloud/ssh to egress-nodes):
   grep "handshake timeout" /var/log/egress/*.log | tail -n 120
   -> snippets: "handshake timeout after 8000ms" from node eu-west-3b, repeated at 13:10-13:12. Also sporadic "kvcache: miss mismatch seq=1245 expected=1240".

Raw error snippets I copied: (real-ish but redacted)
- ERROR [2026-03-09T13:11:07Z] egress: handshake timeout (peer=10.3.12.7:443) policy=regional-handoff v=93
- WARN  [2026-03-09T13:12:31Z] kvcache: key-hash mismatch: key=route-agg:abc seq=1245 expected=1240
- INFO  [2026-03-09T13:13:45Z] retry: increment try=2 cause="upstream reset" route=r123

Immediate observations / notes:
- The kvcache mismatch stands out. If nodes have divergent KV state during a policy update, handoff decisions might do extra validation rounds causing head-of-line delay.
- Handshake timeouts correlate with a small subset of egress nodes (eu-west-3b, us-east-2c). Hardware noise? Network flapping?
- We saw policy-version churn: some agents applied v94 while others still at v92 for ~10-12s. Could be race in rollout push.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Race in policy rollout + stale kvcache -> transient double-checks/validation causing extra RTT. (High plausibility)
2) Asymmetric routing weights + simultaneous autoscaling causing contention on a subset of backends (hot nodes overloaded). (Medium)
3) Intermittent network issue (routing mesh) causing TCP handshakes to frequently reset on certain AZs. (Medium-low)
4) Instrumentation/metrics artifact: delays are in control-plane handoff path, not model compute. (Low for this incident given egress logs)

Commands and small experiments to isolate:
- reproduce trace with X-Force TTL disabled (to force cache misses) and compare latency:
  routectl set feature ttl-heuristic=false --route r123 --apply && run locust for 3m
- force single-version policy rollout to a subset:
  routectl rollout --route r123 --version v94 --target eu-west-3b --serial 1s
- perform synthetic handshake stress on suspect node to see whether kernel drops:
  for i in {1..200}; do nc -vz 10.3.12.7 443; sleep 0.05; done 2>&1 | tee hc.out

Notes from run (hc.out):
- ~6% of connection attempts reset with "Connection refused" in a burst at ~13:10 window.

Things to check/next actions (todo with owners):
- [ ] Confirm KV write durability during rollout (Marcus). Is the KV propagation using async replication that could cause seq divergence?
- [ ] Check kernel/sysctl dmesg spikes on eu-west-3b (Sofia). Look for NIC driver errors, rps/tx queue drops.
- [ ] Replay policy rollout in canary infra and trace per-node policy-apply times (me). Add more logging around apply ack latency.
- [ ] Add a short-term guard: require policy apply ack from N nodes before promoting next policy stage (ops proposal). (me + infra)

Random hypotheses I want to remember:
- If KV sequencer increments on write but consumer applies out-of-order due to replay queue length, we might see expected!=actual. Could be caused by heavy GC or compaction pause in our KV store.
- The handshake timeouts could be due to ephemeral overloading of the TLS hardware accelerator on some box types under burst. Cross-check instance types on failing nodes.

Short-term mitigation tried:
- Immediate rollback to v92 stabilized tail latency. That's consistent with rollout/order causing the issue.
- We also temporarily excluded eu-west-3b from ingress rotation which made errors disappear for that region (manual routing override).

Logs/artefacts to attach to ticket: call out these log lines, routectl outputs, and hc.out. See linked_artifacts for ticket/PR drafts.

Notes to self before handing over: write a small test to simulate policy-version churn with artificially delayed apply acks and KV inconsistencies. If reproducible, duplicate in staging and test rollback guard change.

End of scratchpad.

- Jia
